newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in dull late trading on Friday, with liquidity remaining stable, dealers said.
They said operators seemed to wind down for the weekend.
"There was not much activity today. People just squared positions ahead of the weekend," one local bank dealer said.
One Japanese bank dealer said operators appeared to remain cautious, with short-dated swap rates hovering at high level.
He said operators might be worried over the liquidity outlook on Monday, with sustained buying interest keeping tom/next swap rate traded at 0.62/0.65 points.
Overnight swap closed at 2.1/2.4. Overnight money was last traded at around 16.5 percent late in the afternoon.
The local bank dealer said players seemed to be reluctant to be exposed to short dollar positions ahead of the weekend, keeping some support for dollars at around 2,323.0 level.
"I would rather go slightly long or stay squared," he said.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,323.4/24.4 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,324.0/24.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,323.0/24.0 and 2,320.0/21.5, respectively.
Dealers said sentiment was firm on the rupiah but some said the dollar might have bottomed out for now.
They said longer-term swap rates were little changed.
One-month swap was quoted at 17.5/18.0, two at 34.0/35.5, three at 52.0/53.0 and six at 100.5/101.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,317/2,509 and the conversion rate at 2,317/2,365 on Friday.
